newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU ACCEPTS 472,000 TONNES SOFT WHEAT EXPORT.
newsitem.headline: EU ACCEPTS 472,000 TONNES SOFT WHEAT EXPORT.

text.p: The European Union said on Thursday it had provisionally accepted export bids for 472,000 tonnes of soft wheat grain at an export tax of three Ecus per tonne.
The bids were submitted before the Commission's decision overnight to raise the export tax for the second time in a week to six Ecus to discourage excessive demand for licences.
"We have in principle accepted 472,000 tonnes which were bid for on Tuesday and Wednesday," a European Commission spokesman in Brussels said.
The Commission officially has three working days to decide whether to use a veto on bids for standing refunds or taxes.
It was not immediately clear to what extent the Commission intended the unusual caveat involved in its acceptance of the bids to be seen as a warning that they could still founder.
It has used a similar device before to signal its intentions at times of market turmoil, but one official insisted that accepting the current bids was still only a "possibility".
The spokesman said the Commission had decided to raise taxes in the hope that the volume of bids would subside after a hectic week which has seen over a million tonnes of bids tossed out.
